history.period: 8th century CE (inscription-based); debated - some historians date it to the 5th century
history.summary: Ancient Vishnu temple at the Triveni Sangam in Rajim, dated to the 8th century CE by an undated inscription of Vilasatunga of the Nala dynasty (dated by paleography); a second inscription is dated 1145 CE and refers to a temple of the mythical king Jagat Pal. Alexander Cunningham dated it to the 5th century, in which case the Nala inscription would refer to a restoration rather than construction; other sources place it between the 7th and 8th centuries. The temple sits in a courtyard with four subsidiary shrines, and consists of a mandapa, antechamber and sanctum under a shikhara, noted for elaborately carved doorways, pillars and pilasters depicting Hindu gods and goddesses, including Vamana, Trivikrama and Narasimha sculptures. Local legend holds that the idol was found by 'Rajim Telin', an oil-seller devotee of Vishnu. The temple has been renovated repeatedly over the centuries (Maratha, Bhonsle, and 1941 restoration by the Raja of Raipur). It is the venue of the annual Rajim Kumbh during Magh Purnima. District note: Rajim is officially in Gariaband district (proposed to move to Raipur district).

name: Rajiv Lochan Temple
town_description: Rajim is an ancient pilgrimage town at the Triveni Sangam of the Mahanadi, Pairi and Sondur rivers, called the 'Prayag of Chhattisgarh'. Named after the Rajiv Lochan Mandir, it is officially in Gariaband district (proposed for Raipur district), about 45-50 km from Raipur, with a 2011 census population of about 14,090. The town hosts the annual Rajim Kumbh Mela and is regarded as the cultural capital of Chhattisgarh.
